name: Adaeus of Mitylene
bio: Adaeus of Mitylene is one of the epigrammatists whose short poems were gathered in the Greek Anthology. Paton's index of authors dates the poet to 1st century AD. Paton's index lists the poet among the writers of the Wreath of Philippus, the Garland compiled in the first century AD.
This archive carries the 5 epigrams ascribed to the poet in the second volume of W. R. Paton's prose translation (Book VII: 51, 238, 240, 305, 694).

poems.title: Book VII, 51: On the Same
poems.author: Adaeus of Mitylene
poems.text: Neither dogs slew thee, Euripides, nor the rage of women, thou enemy of the secrets of Cypris, but Death and old age, and under Macedonian Arethusa thou liest, honoured by the friendship of Archelaus. Yet it is not this that I account thy tomb, but the altar of Bacchus and the buskin-trodden stage.

poems.title: Book VII, 238
poems.author: Adaeus of Mitylene
poems.text: I, Pyrrhus, who first set the steps of Macedonia in the path of war, lie here clothed in the earth of Aegae. No king before me did such deeds, and if any have greater to boast of, it is because he is of my blood.

poems.title: Book VII, 240
poems.author: Adaeus of Mitylene
poems.text: If one would sing of the tomb of Alexander of Macedon, let him say that both continents are his monument.

poems.title: Book VII, 305
poems.author: Adaeus of Mitylene
poems.text: The fisherman, Diotimus, whose boat, one and the same, was his faithful bearer at sea and on land the abode of his penury, fell into the sleep from which there is no awakening, and rowing himself, came to relentless Hades in his own ship; for the boat that had supported the old man in life paid him its last service in death too by being the wood for his pyre.

poems.title: Book VII, 694: Not Sepulchral
poems.author: Adaeus of Mitylene
poems.text: If thou passest by the shrine of the hero (his name is Philopragmon) that is at the cross-roads outside Potidaea, tell him on what task thou journeyest, and he at once will help thee to find a means of accomplishing it.
